definitions.name: input data
definitions.choice: Start from the processed figshare files (10.6084/m9.figshare.26131789.v1, slidetags.tar.xz, md5 65bb74092f73ab7f7f061390a6e35030): SCP2167.h5ad (humancortex), SCP2169.h5ad (HumanTonsil), SCP2170.h5ad (mouseembryo), SCP2171.h5ad (HumanMelanomaRNA), SCP2176.h5ad (HumanMelanomaMultiome). These are the adata.h5ad written by notebook cell 8 (filtered, normalised, with the 9 method results in .uns).
definitions.quote: Methods: "we used five processed and recently published spatially informed single nucleus RNA sequencing (slide-tags) datasets41."
definitions.ambiguity: The raw Single Cell Portal data need a login (401), so the preprocessing in cell 8 (barcode match to the spatial table, filter_cells min_genes=200, filter_genes min_cells=3, normalize_total 1e4 + log1p) is NOT re-checked. SCP2162 (mouse hippocampus) is excluded in the notebook ("barcodes between metadata and matrix do not match"); the paper says five datasets, consistent. The run must confirm with anndata that .X is log-normalised, layers["raw"] holds counts, obsm["spatial"] exists and .uns has the 9 method keys.

definitions.name: evaluation layers
definitions.choice: Layer A (primary): authors' method outputs adata.uns[<method>] as published + Moran truth recomputed by us + authors' evaluation code (notebook cells 12-13, utils.py). Layer B (secondary, only if the light-mode budget allows): re-run the 9 methods from .X with the cell 8 settings, compare the new .uns with the published one, then repeat A.
definitions.quote: Methods: "Then we ran all ligand-receptor methods in LIANA+ without taking spatial information into account."
definitions.ambiguity: The authors ran cell 8 with n_jobs=10; light mode caps us at 4 processes/threads, so layer B uses n_jobs=4. Whether n_jobs changes the permutation stream in liana 1.0.5 is not known before the run; any .uns difference is reported, not tuned away.

Resource "consensus" (human) / "mouseconsensus" (mouse), bundled in the wheel.
definitions.quote: Code availability: "We used LIANA+ v1.0.5 release for the analyses presented here." Notebook cell 2 prints li.__version__ = '1.0.5'.
definitions.ambiguity: env.yml is the full lab env; the notebook kernel name "spiana" matches it (python 3.10.13). spiana.yml in the same folder (python 3.10.10, decoupler 1.5.1) is the laptop env and is not used. An optional liana 2.0.0 run is only a robustness note, never the main reading.

definitions.name: spatial weights for the truth
definitions.choice: li.ut.spatial_neighbors(adata, bandwidth=150, cutoff=0.1, set_diag=True), default kernel "gaussian" w = exp(-d^2 / (2 l^2)), coordinates obsm["spatial"].
definitions.quote: Methods: "Throughout the manuscript, unless otherwise specified, we used Gaussian weights with a bandwidth of 150 and a cut-off of 0.1, and the diagonal (self to self) was set to 1 for the local scores."
definitions.ambiguity: None between text and code. Coordinate units are whatever the SCP spatial table had (not re-checked, see D01).

definitions.name: ligand-receptor co-localisation (lrdata)
definitions.choice: li.mt.lr_bivar(adata, function_name="morans", use_raw=False, n_perms=1000, expr_prop=0.05, mask_negatives=True, resource_name=consensus|mouseconsensus, seed default 1337). Uses global Moran's R (lrdata.var["morans_r"]) and its one-sided permutation p-value (lrdata.var["morans_pvals"], one-sided because mask_negatives=True).
definitions.quote: Methods: "we estimated global Moran's R using LIANA+ to generate an indirect ground truth-that is, ligand-receptors and cell types co-localized to a greater extend than random (Moran's R >0 and FDR <0.05)."
definitions.ambiguity: Methods (bivariate metrics) says interactions not expressed in at least 10% of spots are excluded "by default"; the notebook overrides with expr_prop=0.05. Follow the notebook. The truth files (lrdata/cpdata) were not published, so they are recomputed; there is no published per-item truth to check them against.

definitions.name: cell-type co-localisation (cpdata)
definitions.choice: ctdata = utils.onehot_groupby(adata, "cell_type") (one-hot float32, obsm/obsp copied); li.mt.lr_bivar(ctdata, function_name="morans", use_raw=False, expr_prop=0, n_perms=1000, mask_negatives=True, interactions=all ordered pairs of cell types). Self pairs (autocrine) are removed by liana ("Removing 7 self-interactions" in the authors' output for humancortex), so autocrine cell-type pairs drop out of the evaluation through the inner join.
definitions.quote: Notebook cell 10: "# Run CP; NOTE: I'm currently discarding autocrine, and only evaluating para/ortho".
definitions.ambiguity: The paper text does not say autocrine pairs are excluded; the code does. Follow the code.

definitions.name: truth threshold (MAIN READING R0 = code)
definitions.choice: Exactly utils.join_pred_truth: lr_truth = (p_adjust_fdr(morans_pvals <= 0.05)) * (morans_r > 0); same for ct_truth; truth = lr_truth * ct_truth. Note the parenthesis: p_adjust_fdr receives the BOOLEAN (pvals <= 0.05), not the p-values. With decoupler 1.6.0 p_adjust_fdr (BH via np.asfarray, cumulative minimum, capped at 1) a 0/1 input comes back unchanged, so the code truth is (raw permutation p <= 0.05) AND (R > 0), with no FDR correction.
definitions.quote: Methods: "(Moran's R >0 and FDR <0.05)". utils.py: lr_truth['lr_truth'] = ((p_adjust_fdr((lr_truth['morans_pvals']) <= 0.05)) * (lr_truth['morans_r'] > 0)).astype(np.int8)
definitions.ambiguity: Text says FDR < 0.05; the code effectively uses unadjusted p <= 0.05. This text/code difference was NOT in the triage list (triage wrote "verdade = FDR(p) <= 0.05"); found here by reading utils.py and decoupler-py 1.6.0 decoupler/utils.py p_adjust_fdr. The main reading follows the code (it produced the Source Data). Alternative reading V4 applies BH-FDR to the p-values (p_adjust_fdr(morans_pvals) < 0.05).

definitions.name: joining predictions and truth
definitions.choice: Inner join of adata.uns[method] on (ligand_complex, receptor_complex) = lrdata.var (ligand, receptor), then on (source, target) = cpdata.var (ligand, receptor) renamed to source/target. Only rows present in both truths are evaluated.
definitions.ambiguity: Not described in the paper text. Follow the code.

definitions.name: AUROC per scoring function
definitions.choice: For each method, score keys = li.mt.show_methods() "Magnitude Score" and "Specificity Score" (None dropped). gt = li.method.process_scores(gt, score_key) (scores where lower is better, e.g. p-values and ranks, become -log10(x + eps)); AUROC = sklearn roc_auc_score(truth, score) over the whole joined table.
definitions.quote: Methods: "AUROC was calculated for the whole distribution of each ligand-receptor method's scoring functions."
definitions.ambiguity: Score labels: expr_prod is renamed "Product*" for Connectome and "Product✳" for NATMI (notebook cell 18). The AUROC of Product*, Product✳, lr_gmeans and lrscore is expected to be (near-)identical per dataset because they are monotone transforms of the same product; the source-data medians agree to 7 decimals (0.5292327).

definitions.name: false-positive filters (MAIN READING R0 = code, notebook cell 12)
definitions.choice: CellPhoneDB: cellphone_pvals < 0.05. Connectome: ligand_pvals < 0.05 & receptor_pvals < 0.05 & scaled_weight > 0. log2FC: ligand_pvals < 0.05 & receptor_pvals < 0.05 & lr_logfc > 0. NATMI: spec_weight > quantile(gt.spec_weight, 0.95). SingleCellSignalR: lrscore > 0.6. Rank_Aggregate: magnitude_rank < 0.05 & specificity_rank < 0.05. Geometric Mean: gmean_pvals < 0.05. scSeqComm: inter_score > 0.95. CellChat: cellchat_pvals < 0.05 & (ligand_pvals < 0.05 | receptor_pvals < 0.05). Applied to the joined table gt before process_scores.
definitions.quote: Methods: "For CellPhoneDB, CellChat and Geometric mean, interactions with P values below 0.05 were filtered. ... For LIANA's rank aggregate, we kept only those with a magnitude rank <0.05. Since the authors of NATMI and scSeqComm do not suggest a threshold, we kept interactions if they were within the top 5% of the specificity weight and interscore distributions, respectively."
definitions.ambiguity: Two text/code differences, run as alternative readings: V2 Rank_Aggregate with magnitude_rank < 0.05 only (text); V3 scSeqComm top 5% = inter_score > quantile(gt.inter_score, 0.95) (text, same form as the NATMI filter) instead of the absolute cut 0.95. Neither is decided from numbers; the Source Data rows were produced by the code, which is why the code is the main reading.

definitions.name: balanced accuracy, precision, recall, positive calls
definitions.choice: On the binary filter of D10: sklearn balanced_accuracy_score(truth, binary, adjusted=False), precision_score, recall_score; Positive Calls = binary.sum() / number of rows of gt. One value per method per dataset (repeated on both score rows of a method in the Source Data).
definitions.ambiguity: For Fig. 4b,d the per-method median is taken over the 5 datasets with one value per dataset; the duplicated rows give the same median, as the notebook groupby("Method").median() does. Checked in the Source Data: both score rows of a method carry identical BA/F1n values.

definitions.name: normalised F1 (per method, Fig. 4d) and its random baseline (MAIN READING R0 = code)
definitions.choice: F1 = sklearn f1_score(truth, binary, average="binary"); baseline = utils.generate_random_baseline: rng = np.random.default_rng(seed=42), 1000 successive permutations of the binary column (each permutes the already-permuted vector), mean F1 over them; F1 (normalised) = (F1 / baseline) / 2. A new rng with seed 42 is created on every call.
definitions.quote: Methods: "Normalized F1 = 1/2 (F1observed / F1permuted) where 'observed' is the F1 score for the actual ligand-receptor predictions, while the 'permuted' F1 was generated by shuffling the predictions of each method (100 times) and calculating an F1 score."
definitions.ambiguity: Text says 100 shuffles, code uses n_perms=1000. Main reading = code; alternative V1 = 100 permutations (same seed 42, same procedure). The Fig. 4 legend says normalised F1 "is bound between negative and positive infinity" while the formula is >= 0; text-only issue, no effect on numbers.

definitions.name: normalised F1* (per score, Fig. 4c)
definitions.choice: After process_scores: cap = (score >= np.quantile(score, 0.95)); F1* = f1_score(truth, cap); baseline as D12 on the cap column (1000 permutations, seed 42); F1* (normalised) = (F1* / baseline) / 2.
definitions.quote: Methods: "Similarly, when evaluating the individual scoring functions from each method, we considered only the top 5% as positive predictions."
definitions.ambiguity: With ties at the 95th quantile more than 5% can be positive (notebook comment: "not really possible due to ties"); follow the code (>=). The 100-vs-1000 permutation variant V1 also applies here.

definitions.name: aggregation and ordering
definitions.choice: Per-score (AUROC, F1*n) or per-method (BA, F1n) median over the 5 datasets (plain median of 5 values); order = descending median, as the figure orders boxes by groupby(x).median().
definitions.quote: Fig. 4 legend: "The boxes were ordered according to the median performance across datasets (central line in cyan within each box; n = 5 datasets)."
definitions.ambiguity: With 5 datasets a change in one dataset row can move a median directly, so per-row results (R75) are reported before medians.

definitions.name: randomness and determinism
definitions.choice: liana 1.0.5 default seed 1337 (liana/_constants.py DefaultValues.seed) for the Moran permutations; seed 42 for the F1 baselines. No seed is changed. Light mode: nice -n 19, OMP/MKL/OPENBLAS/NUMEXPR threads = 4, at most 4 processes, CPU only.
definitions.quote: Not in the paper; from the liana 1.0.5 source and utils.py.
definitions.ambiguity: Permutation p-values (1000 permutations) near the 0.05 cut can flip if the random stream differs (numpy/numba version, thread count); that moves truth labels and AUROC at the 3rd decimal. Since no truth was published, if layer A misses the exact tier we report how many LR pairs and cell-type pairs have p within 0.005 of the cut, instead of guessing which labels differ.
